title: Why coding agents lose project requirements between sessions
body: Claude context window limitations require persisting requirements and state to disk files across sessions. Because context memory is bounded per invocation, durable state must be serialized to repo artifacts.
symptom: Autonomous coding agent forgets user requirements and architecture rules when starting a new session turn
root_cause: Context window limits cause conversation truncation; unbounded multi-turn dialog loses project requirements without file serialization
remedy: Serialize architectural constraints and progress ledger to version-controlled markdown artifacts read at session startup
evidence_excerpt: Claude context window limitations require persisting requirements and state to disk files across sessions.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Official vendor documentation confirms context memory boundaries require disk-persisted state artifacts.

title: MCP function call fails because tool JSON schema mismatches payload
body: Model Context Protocol JSON-RPC specification requires tool call parameters to validate against declared JSON schema. Type mismatches, unexpected properties, or missing required fields cause protocol validation errors.
symptom: Agent tool invocation crashes with invalid parameter protocol error when calling external MCP server
root_cause: Tool input arguments deviate from strict JSON Schema declarations; missing required keys or schema type mismatch triggers server rejection
remedy: Enforce client-side schema validation using pydantic or declarative filters before dispatching tool execution payloads
evidence_excerpt: Model Context Protocol JSON-RPC specification requires tool call parameters to validate against declared JSON schema.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Official specification document confirms JSON-RPC protocol rejection upon schema deviation.

title: Configuring sandbox permission boundaries for autonomous coding agents
body: Security architecture for coding agent CLIs enforces read-only sandbox execution boundaries, file system path validation, and shell execution permission gates to prevent unauthorized write mutations.
symptom: Unconstrained coding agent modifies git internals or executes unsafe destructive shell commands outside workspace root
root_cause: Permissive subshell execution grants unvalidated write access to host directories without path-scoping and namespace boundaries
remedy: Enforce pre-execution path validation, unshare network namespaces, and block path traversal using strict sandbox limits
evidence_excerpt: Security architecture for coding agent CLIs enforces read-only sandbox execution boundaries, file system path validation, and shell execution permission gates to prevent unauthorized write mutations.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Official engineering documentation mandates sandbox execution boundaries and permission gates.

title: Evaluating coding agent completion reliability without cherry-picked benchmarks
body: SWE-bench benchmark evaluation harness provides reproducible test matrices across real-world repository tasks, evaluating autonomous issue resolution rates against ground-truth unit test suites.
symptom: Benchmarked coding agent claims high task resolution in synthetic demos but repeatedly fails on real-world multi-file bugfixes
root_cause: Synthetic single-turn unit tests fail to evaluate regression prevention, execution feedback loops, and repo-scale dependency management
remedy: Evaluate agent task completion against multi-file real repository benchmarks using SWE-bench with ground-truth test verification
evidence_excerpt: SWE-bench benchmark evaluation harness provides reproducible test matrices across real-world repository tasks, evaluating autonomous issue resolution rates against ground-truth unit test suites.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Peer-reviewed benchmark methodology independently confirms synthetic test suites inflate agent reliability.

title: Git Worktree Isolation: Preventing Multi-Agent File Contention and Race Conditions
body: Running multiple autonomous subagents against a shared Git repository causes index locking and file write collisions. Git worktrees create isolated working directories linked to a single object store.
symptom: Concurrent coding agents fail when executing git commands due to index.lock file collisions
root_cause: Git repositories permit only one process to hold the index lock at a time; parallel agents editing the same working tree clash
remedy: Spawn subagents in isolated git worktrees sharing the common object repository via git worktree add
evidence_excerpt: A git worktree allows multiple working trees attached to the same repository.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Git core specification confirms worktree isolation avoids index locking collisions.
